title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors of Ansell; senior management, being all members of the executive leadership team and all employees with Vice President designation; and any employee with access to the monthly consolidated financial information or otherwise likely to receive price sensitive or Inside Information who is notified as such by the Company Secretary. Subject to Trading Windows, Clearance, the short-term dealing ban, the margin loan prohibition and ad-hoc restrictions.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All directors of Ansell. Clearance is given by the Chairman of the Board (or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board's own dealing), and directors must notify the Company of changes in their security interests for Listing Rule purposes.

tiers.name: ELT Members
tiers.description: All members of the executive leadership team. Designated Persons whose Clearance, and that of the Company Secretary, is given by the Managing Director/CEO.

tiers.name: Vice Presidents
tiers.description: All employees with Vice President designation. Designated Persons cleared by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Designated Employees
tiers.description: Any employee with access to the monthly consolidated financial information and any other employees likely to receive price sensitive or Inside Information in the course of their positions who are notified as such by the Company Secretary. Cleared by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: All directors, senior executives and employees (and their associates) to whom the Policy applies. Those who are not Designated Persons are bound by the insider trading rules, the front page test and, if plan participants, the clause 5.3 hedging prohibition, but not by Trading Windows, Clearance or the margin loan prohibition.

tiers.name: Closely Related Parties
tiers.description: Spouse, partner or dependent child (including adult and step-children); a relative residing with the Designated Person; another family member the Designated Person may be expected to influence or be influenced by in relation to Dealings in Ansell Securities; and companies, trusts, partnerships and other entities that the Designated Person or any of those persons control or significantly influence. Trading Windows and Clearance apply to them, and the Designated Person must do any required act on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to a security granted under the relevant plan and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those Securities, while the Securities remain unvested. Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a 'profit' in those Securities.

windows.start_anchor: commencement of trading on the ASX on the second trading day after the release of the Company's half-yearly results to the ASX
commencement of trading on the ASX on the second trading day after the release of the Company's annual results to the ASX
commencement of trading on the ASX on the second trading day after the holding of the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company, in its sole and absolute discretion, may impose additional restrictions on Dealing by all or any Designated Persons, expressly including where a Trading Window is otherwise open. Any such restriction communicated to Designated Persons must be kept strictly confidential. The Trading Windows themselves also operate only 'unless the Company advises otherwise'.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule for vested holdings. Dealing expressly extends to forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities, and to agreements to do any of those things, so an OTC put and written call are Dealings. A Designated Person may therefore enter them only inside a 30-day Trading Window, with written Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer valid for five trading days, and only if not in possession of Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Dealing in Securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling Securities. It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over Ansell shares are Securities (the definition expressly includes options and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market) and are treated identically to OTC derivatives: Trading Window plus five trading day Clearance.
rules.evidence: The definition of securities in the Corporations Act is very broad, and includes shares, options, debentures, convertible notes and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Writing put or call options over the underlying Securities and Dealing in derivative products are expressly named as prohibited conduct for all participants in an approved share or equity plan while the plan Securities remain unvested. The ban applies to every plan participant, not only Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a 'profit' in those Securities.

rules.detail: Purpose-based prohibition on any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value of a plan security and remove the element of price risk while it remains unvested. The list of prohibited conduct is expressly non-exhaustive, so economically equivalent structures are caught.
rules.evidence: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to a security granted under the relevant plan and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those Securities, while the Securities remain unvested.

rules.detail: Clause 5.3 is keyed to Securities that 'remain unvested' and clause 5.2 separately refers to 'the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods', so plan shares that have vested but are still within a restriction period are not expressly covered by the hedging ban. The underlying plan rules, which are not part of this Policy, would need to be checked.

The clause 5.3 hedging prohibition stops at vesting, and hedging Securities is expressly a Dealing. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares is therefore permitted for a Designated Person inside a Trading Window with Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer, subject to the front page test which is an express ground for refusing approval.
rules.evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

rules.detail: An employee who is not a Designated Person and whose plan securities have vested is not restricted by clause 5.3 and is not subject to Trading Windows or Clearance; only the insider trading prohibition and the front page test apply.

Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts are expressly within the definition of Dealing, so a prepaid forward or similar requires a Trading Window and Clearance. If the monetisation is funded by a loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities, clause 4.8 says a Designated Person should not enter into it.
rules.evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities. It also extends to entering into an agreement to do any of the above.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no short selling prohibition and does not use the term; a short sale would still be a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance for a Designated Person, and would sit uneasily with the short-term dealing ban.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere and is not listed in the definition of Dealing.

CFDs are not named. They are derivative products over Ansell Securities and so a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance, but the clause 4.6 prohibition on short-term trading, including within 3 months of receiving Securities, would in practice preclude typical CFD activity.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities

rules.detail: A CFD over unvested plan securities is Dealing in a derivative product that removes price risk and is expressly prohibited conduct under clause 5.3.
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products

rules.detail: A one-line prohibition covering margin loans and 'similar funding arrangements' in respect of Ansell Securities, with no vesting-state or amount qualification. It is expressed as 'should' rather than 'must', and clause 4.5 gives Authorising Officers discretion to approve Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, so a waiver route is arguably available.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Clause 4.8 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons and does not apply to other employees.

Granting security over Ansell Securities is not named and is not listed in the definition of Dealing. The Policy nevertheless contemplates that security agreements over Ansell Securities exist, since clause 4.4(a)(v) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement as an Excluded Dealing. An encumbrance forming part of a margin loan or similar funding arrangement is caught by clause 4.8.

Clause 4.8 reaches beyond margin loans to any 'similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company', which on its face captures a bank loan drawn against and secured on Ansell shares as part of a collar. There is no dedicated waiver in clause 4.8 itself, but clause 4.5 permits an Authorising Officer to approve Dealings otherwise prohibited by the Policy.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: No secured financing restriction applies to employees who are not Designated Persons.

No short-term trading, including trading within 3 months of receiving the Securities, except in limited circumstances (severe financial hardship, dealings of long term incentive Securities upon vesting, or a legal obligation to sell or transfer) and with the approval of the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities

clearance.approver: Authorising Officer per clause 4.3(d): Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board; Chairman of the Board for Directors and the Managing Director/CEO; Managing Director/CEO for ELT Members and the Company Secretary; Company Secretary for Vice Presidents and Designated Employees
clearance.post_trade_to: relevant Authorising Officer, after any Excluded Dealing under clause 4.4
clearance.evidence: If a Clearance is given to Deal, the clearance will be confirmed in writing and will be valid for a period of five trading days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated. No Dealing by a Designated Person may be executed beyond the five day period referred to in paragraph (b) without having sought and received further Clearance.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee where the dealer is the Chair of the Board)
clearance.post_trade_to: the Company (change in security interests, for Listing Rule notification)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as possible, to enable the Company to comply with the Listing Rule timeframes
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify the Company if there is a change in their security interests as soon as possible to enable the Company to comply with relevant timeframes under the Listing Rules

clearance.approver: The Authorising Officer of the associated Designated Person, who must obtain the Clearance on the Closely Related Party's behalf
clearance.evidence: Where this Policy requires a Closely Related Party to do an act (for example provide a notification or obtain a Clearance), you must do that act on behalf of your Closely Related Party.

financing_disclosure: Designated Persons; trigger: undertaking any Excluded Dealing, including a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement; to the relevant Authorising Officer under clause 4.3(d); no deadline stated

external_documents: Ansell director and employee security plan, performance rights plan and option plan rules (referenced for vesting and restriction periods, not attached)
exemption_authority: Clause 4.5: in exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officers in clause 4.3(d) have discretion to approve Dealings outside a Trading Window or to approve Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, assessed case by case, in absolute discretion without reasons, withdrawable if new information comes to light, and to be kept strictly confidential. Clause 4.6 gives the Company Secretary a separate approval power for exceptions to the 3 month short-term dealing rule.
jurisdiction_overlays: Clause 3.6 requires compliance with insider trading rules or law globally in relation to Securities of other listed entities

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan and similar funding ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities and so within clause 4.8, which is the principal obstacle; note the hortatory 'should' rather than 'must not'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officers listed in clause 4.3(d) have discretion to approve Dealings by the respective Designated Person in Ansell Securities outside a Trading Window, or to approve Dealings in Ansell Securities that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, an Authorising Officer can approve dealings that the policy otherwise prohibits, so the funded collar is not structurally impossible; the whole structure would need Board Chair or CEO level sign-off as an exceptional circumstance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may at any time, without seeking Clearance ... dispose of Ansell Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates secured lending over Ansell shares and protects the executive if the bank enforces or takes delivery outside a Trading Window, requiring only after-the-event notice to the Authorising Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value ... while the Securities remain unvested.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is bounded by vesting rather than by any holding lock, so vested plan shares are available for a collar, subject to the Trading Window and Clearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Closely Related Parties may, unless the Company advises otherwise, Deal in Ansell Securities during the 30-day period beginning ... on the second trading day after [half-yearly results / annual results / the AGM]. ... Designated Persons may not Deal in Ansell Securities outside the Trading Windows.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-window policy: entry, roll and unwind of the collar must each fall inside one of only three 30-day windows a year, which constrains tenor selection and expiry dates.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the clearance will be confirmed in writing and will be valid for a period of five trading days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated. No Dealing ... may be executed beyond the five day period ... without having sought and received further Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and signing of the derivative legs must complete within five trading days of Clearance, and a staged or averaged execution beyond that needs fresh Clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company, in its sole and absolute discretion, may impose additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place when a Trading Window is open. Any restriction ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open window is never a guarantee; a confidential ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry or unwind without the bank being told why.

bespoke_clauses.topic: front page test as a refusal ground
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval under this Policy is required for a Dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express mandatory ground for refusing Clearance, and a senior executive hedging a stake with bank funding is squarely the kind of transaction it targets.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Related Parties are aware of, and comply with, this Policy. Where this Policy requires a Closely Related Party to do an act ... you must do that act on behalf of your Closely Related Party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a controlled trust or company does not avoid clause 4.8 or the Clearance requirement, and the Designated Person must obtain Clearance on the entity's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collaring shares within three months of vesting or acquisition risks breaching clause 4.6 unless the Company Secretary approves, so the parcel selection should favour older holdings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any sale of Ansell shares acquired by a Designated Person under any Ansell share or equity plan (at the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods or upon exercise of options) must only occur during a Trading Window ... and with Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the call leg over plan-sourced shares is a sale that must itself fall inside a Trading Window with fresh Clearance, so expiry dates should be aligned to the windows or the collar cash settled.

summary: A funded collar is possible at Ansell only as an approved exception, not as of right. The derivative legs over vested, unrestricted shares are permissible in principle: the clause 5.3 hedging prohibition stops at vesting, and hedging, granting options and forward contracts are expressly Dealings, so a Designated Person needs written Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer, valid five trading days, executed inside one of the three 30-day Trading Windows that open on the second trading day after the half-yearly results, the annual results and the AGM, with no inside information and subject to the mandatory front page test. The loan leg runs into clause 4.8, under which no Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities, which on its face captures a loan drawn against the collared shares. The saving feature is clause 4.5: in exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer may approve Dealings outside a Trading Window or Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, so a Chair or CEO level approval could in principle sanction the structure, and clause 4.4(a)(v) already treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement as an Excluded Dealing needing no Clearance. Practical constraints remain: confidential ad-hoc restrictions can override an open window, the 3 month rule after receiving Securities, and physical settlement of the call over plan-sourced shares must itself fall inside a Trading Window with fresh Clearance.
